title: A New Garden at Maple Street School
source: Original passage written for this demonstration (no ReadWorks content)
content:
Students at Maple Street School spent Saturday morning digging, planting, and watering. By noon, the empty patch of grass behind the gym had become a garden.

About forty children and twenty parents joined the project. They built six wooden beds and filled them with soil from the town's compost center. Then they planted tomatoes, carrots, beans, lettuce, and sunflowers.

"I have never grown anything before," said fourth grader Omar Rahman. "I put in the carrot seeds myself. I hope they come up soon."

The idea began last fall, when Ms. Alvarez's science class asked a question: where does our lunch come from? The class wrote letters to local businesses, and a hardware store gave the wood. A nursery donated the seedlings.

Each class will take care of one bed. Students will water the plants, pull weeds, and keep a journal about how the plants change. In the fall, the vegetables will be used in the school cafeteria, and anything extra will go to the town food pantry.

Principal Grant Wilson thanked everyone who helped. "This garden is a classroom without walls," he said. "Children learn science, math, and teamwork here, and they get to taste the results."

The garden will be open to families on Friday afternoons. Visitors are welcome to come and see what is growing.
